A few other people proceeded to ask for some, and I gave them some. Except for one other person who also just launched themselves at me without asking. M then proceeded to pester me and apologize and ask nicely. But I told her she was only saying that because I told her to, and didn't let her have one. I finished them off. Apparently, I'm the asshole for excluding her, but I was just upset that she lunged straight for my food before even acknowledging me. Everyone else I shared with asked. I guess my refusing her as she attempted to ask again is borderline assholery. So, the question is, am I in the right or not? Let's break this down. First, I brought the food, so it's mine. I have the right to decide who gets to have some. I gave some to my friends who asked nicely. Then, M came over and just grabbed for the food without asking. That's not respectful. I pulled them away and told her she couldn't have one. Then, she tried to pester me and apologize, but I still didn't give her any. Is it wrong to exclude someone who didn't ask nicely and just lunged for the food? Or is it reasonable to be upset and not share with someone who was rude? On one hand, sharing food is kind and generous, and I usually do that. But on the other hand, M's behavior was disrespectful. She didn't ask; she just reached over and grabbed for the food. That's not polite. I had every right to be upset and not share with her. But then, after that, she tried to apologize and ask nicely. Should I have given her some then? Maybe I should have given her some to be kind, even though she was initially rude. But I was upset, and I didn't want to share with someone who didn't respect my boundaries. It's important to stand up for yourself and not let people take advantage of your kindness. So, in conclusion, I think I was in the right to refuse M because she was disrespectful by lunging for the food without asking.
